# Donny — Backend Engineer

> Donny (donny eats tech) is a backend engineer specializing in distributed systems, databases, and infrastructure. Currently Senior Software Engineer at Clientell, where he owns the AI-agent execution path and built the Salesforce org-indexing platform. Based in Bengaluru, India. Writes long-form technical deep-dives on Substack.

## About

- **Role:** Senior Software Engineer at Clientell (Oct 2025 – present)
- **Focus:** Backend engineering — distributed systems, databases, infrastructure, observability
- **Location:** Bengaluru, India
- **Core stack:** Go, Python, PostgreSQL, Redis, FastAPI, AWS, GCP, Terraform, Pub/Sub, OpenTelemetry
- **Interests:** Postgres internals, consistent hashing, Raft/consensus, systems programming

## Experience

- **Clientell — Senior Software Engineer (Oct 2025 – present):** Owns reliability for 9 production services and runs the design review that gates the LLM agent execution path on a 10-engineer team. Led the 7-day GCP-to-AWS migration of 9 services (planned 1-hour cutover): rebuilt Pub/Sub delivery semantics on SNS+SQS (visibility-timeout redelivery, DLQs), kept consumers idempotent under at-least-once delivery, gated the cutover on drained queues. Built the Salesforce org-indexing platform as a phased fan-out pipeline (orchestrator-worker, 28k work items/run, up to 100 workers), cutting the agent's read-tool latency 5x (4s to 800ms). Built observability and SLOs across all 9 services (time-to-detection from over a day to under 10 minutes), diagnosed a p99 regression to SQLAlchemy sessions held across an async boundary, and put infrastructure under Terraform with PR-gated change control. Clientell is an AI agent for Salesforce deployed across 500+ orgs including Notion, Rakuten, and PwC.
- **Fae — Backend Engineer (Jan 2025 – Oct 2025):** Owned backend, infrastructure and technical direction end to end. Halved payment execution latency (5s to 2.5s); built the centralized RBAC + ABAC authorization service with an audit trail and monthly user-access reviews; rewrote a legacy NestJS monolith as 2 FastAPI microservices with a zero-downtime blue-green cutover.
- **Gida Technologies — Software Engineer (Oct 2022 – Nov 2023):** Built a daily ETL pipeline moving 600k health-insurance records per run from BigQuery into PostgreSQL with source-level segregation and PGP encryption for India's Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM); built backend microservices and REST APIs serving 5,000 concurrent users; automated recurring analyst reporting, saving 20 hours/week.
- **KPMG — Governance, Risk and Compliance Services (Jan 2021 – Nov 2021):** Assessed client standard operating procedures for FMCG and aviation clients and reported process gaps and the resulting operational and compliance risks. Final-semester intern from January 2021, then full-time Analyst from July 2021 on a conversion offer.

## Writing

- [Dynamic Memory Allocation and Its Arch Enemy, Fragmentation](https://donnyeatstech.com/writing/dynamic-memory-allocation-fragmentation/): How malloc on macOS (xzone) and Ubuntu (glibc) lay out memory, glibc chunk headers, and how each allocator deals with fragmentation.
- [Yes, you can store JSONs in Postgres. No, you shouldn't. Well, it depends](https://donnyeatstech.com/writing/should-you-store-jsons-in-postgres/): PostgreSQL JSON/JSONB storage mechanics, TOAST chunking, WAL and MVCC costs, told through a production RCA. Also on Substack.
- [From the Birthday Paradox to Consistent Hashing](https://donnyeatstech.com/writing/from-birthday-paradox-to-consistent-hashing/): A conceptual bridge from probability to load distribution in distributed systems. Also on Substack.

## Projects

- [superlite3](https://github.com/donnyeatstech/superlite3): Single-file embedded database written from scratch in C, modeled on SQLite3. Early: OS layer done, WAL pager in progress.
- [redis-go](https://github.com/donnyeatstech/redis-go): Redis-compatible server in Go — RESP2 protocol, TTL expiry, SQLite-backed durability.
- [mit-6.5840](https://github.com/donnyeatstech/mit-6.5840): MIT's distributed systems course — Raft, MapReduce, and distributed key-value stores.
